title: v0.2.2 release
Fix mrexprSrcrefToLabel() crash from Shiny's #line directive
description:
## Summary

- Fixes `mrexprSrcrefToLabel()` crash (`argument is of length zero`) caused by Shiny's new `sourceUTF8()` wrapping app code with a `#line` directive (rstudio/shiny#4352)
- Handles `srcfilealias` objects where `srcfile$lines` is NULL
- Uses `srcref[7]` (pre-remap line number) to correctly index into wrapped source lines

## Background

After rstudio/shiny#4352, `sourceUTF8()` wraps app code before parsing:

```r
lines <- c(
  "..stacktraceon..({",
  sprintf('#line 1 "%s"', file),
  original_lines,
  "})"
)
```

The `#line 1` directive remaps srcref line numbers to the original file's numbering, but `srcfile$lines` contains the wrapped lines (with 2 extra prefix lines). When `mrexprSrcrefToLabel()` does `lines[srcref[1]]`, it reads the wrong line (2 lines too early), walks backward past line 0, and crashes because `grepl()` on `character(0)` returns `logical(0)`.

## Changes

Three fixes in `mrexprSrcrefToLabel()`:

1. **`srcfilealias` support**: When `srcfile$lines` is NULL, fall back to `srcfile$original$lines`
2. **Pre-remap line numbers**: Use `srcref[7]` (when available and different from `srcref[1]`) to correctly index into the srcfilecopy's lines
3. **While loop guard**: Prevent crash when `firstLine` becomes `character(0)`

These mirror the approach Shiny itself took in [commit df138b91e](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/commit/df138b91e) for the analogous `rassignSrcrefToLabel()` / `rexprSrcrefToLabel()` functions.

## Test plan

- [x] Added 5 new tests for `mrexprSrcrefToLabel()` covering normal srcfilecopy, `#line` directive, `srcfilealias`, not-found fallback, and blank-line-preceded assignments
- [x] Full test suite passes (222 tests)
- [x] Verified the 224-shinymeta app in shinycoreci runs without errors

Closes #130

Experiment with using alternate 'unquote' operator
description:
### For discussion only

There are several issues with our current strategy of

* Using the `!!` operator to mark expressions for shinymeta expansion
* Performing the `!!` expansion in both normal (runtime) and meta (code-gen) modes

https://github.com/rstudio/shinymeta/issues/24
https://github.com/rstudio/shinymeta/issues/53
https://github.com/rstudio/shinymeta/issues/57
https://github.com/rstudio/shinymeta/issues/58

This branch explores the idea of

* Using a different ~operator~ function ~(for now using bquote's `.( )` convention, but that's only for expedience)~, current thinking is `..(x)`, pronounced "dot-dot"
* In normal (runtime) mode, _strip_ the operator instead of expanding it (i.e. `..(data())` becomes `data()` instead of the _result of_ `data()`); in meta (code-gen) mode, expand it

I believe this solves all of the issues above.

Downsides: introducing yet another magical bit of syntax, breaks backwards compatibility with shinymeta early adopters.

title: Reverse direction of buildXXXBundle files arg; tweak substituteMetaReactive
description:
- Change buildXXXBundle's interpretation of `files` to make the
  names the destinations and the values the sources. This makes
  more sense because the sources are more likely to be dynamic
  values, and also semantically it feels more sensible to me
  that the "names" would be used to specify where the files
  should end up.
- Also, the `files` argument wasn't really documented, it is
  now.
- substituteMetaReactive can now take a quoted expression as its
  second argument; removes a bunch of boilerplate in the common
  case that it's just a static chunk of code.

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinymeta)
options(shiny.suppressMissingContextError=TRUE)

input <- list(package = "ggplot2")
output <- list()

downloads <- metaReactive({
  "# Retrieve a year's worth of daily download data"
  cranlogs::cran_downloads(!!input$package, from = Sys.Date() - 365, to = Sys.Date())
})

downloads_rolling <- metaReactive({
  "# Convert daily data to 7 day rolling average"
  !!downloads() %>% mutate(count = zoo::rollapply(count, 7, mean, fill = "extend"))
})

output$plot <- metaRender(renderPlot, {
  ggplot(!!downloads_rolling(), aes(date, count)) + geom_line() + ggtitle("Seven day rolling average")
})

# Only need to provide the output, no dependencies!
expandChain(output$plot())
```

generates:

```r
# Retrieve a year's worth of daily download data
downloads <- cranlogs::cran_downloads("ggplot2", from = Sys.Date() - 365, to = Sys.Date())
# Convert daily data to 7 day rolling average
downloads_rolling <- downloads %>%
  mutate(count = zoo::rollapply(count, 7, mean, fill = "extend"))
ggplot(downloads_rolling, aes(date, count)) + geom_line() + ggtitle("Seven day rolling average")
```

title: Fix #40: non-metaExpr() code evaluated with meta-mode enabled?
description:
Fixes #40.

Introduces a new metaMode state, "mixed" (in addition to TRUE and
FALSE, which we could consider moving to "meta" and "normal").

This new state is entered when a metaReactive2 (or other -2) is
executing in meta mode, and you're outside the metaExpr portion.
If you're in "mixed" and you invoke another metaReactive/2, then
that invocation will happen in FALSE (normal) mode.

One way to think of this is as a state machine, where the nodes
are NORMAL, META, and MIXED, and the edges are withMetaMode,
metaDispatch (i.e. entering a meta-reactive object), and metaExpr.

(The lines marked with ** are the new and exciting edges)

```
Normal ==metaDispatch=> Normal
Normal ==metaExpr=> Normal

Meta ==metaDispatch=> Mixed **
Meta ==metaExpr=> Meta

Mixed ==metaDispatch=> Normal **
Mixed ==metaExpr=> Meta
```

For completeness (because this is the only way out of Normal)
here are the ways withMetaMode() affects the state machine.

```
[Any] ==withMetaMode(TRUE)=> Meta
[Any] ==withMetaMode(FALSE)=> Normal
[Any] ==withMetaMode("mixed")=> Mixed
```

## Breaking change

The `metaMode()` function is unexported. I don't know how you can use it effectively without fully understanding the ramifications of mixed mode; if you call `metaMode()`, are you asking because you're trying to implement something like a `metaReactive` (in which case you should treat "mixed" like FALSE), or something like a `metaExpr` (in which case you should treat "mixed" like TRUE)?

title: Proof-of-concept of more automated version of expandCode
description:
For discussion only.

Instead of this:

    expandCode({
      "# Retrieve data",
      df <- !!df()
      filtered <- !!filtered()
      filtered2 <- !!filtered2()
      !!obs()
      !!output$plot()
    }, patchCalls = list(
      df = quote(df),
      filtered = quote(filtered),
      filtered2 = quote(filtered2)
    ))

You can do this:

    expandObjects(
      "# Retrieve data",
      df,
      filtered,
      filtered2,
      obs,
      output$plot
    )

The only valid arguments to `expandObjects` are `metaObserve' or `metaReactive` objects (passed by bare name), `metaRender` outputs (passed by `output$barename`), or comment strings.

title: Improvements to code formatting:
More aggressively strip unnecessary outer braces
description:
Strip extra outer braces earlier. There are some cases that we
don't currently optimize well after all the code has been expanded,
such as

```r
!!r() %>% filter(whatever)
```

In this case, we end up with `{...}` around the expanded r() code,
because we don't trim in pipeline steps.
